source: Extracted from shipped Layer 2 tax bundle (concierge-assets/main-tax-CWE3nxTZ.js inheritance checklist). English strings unaltered.

items.question: Do your heirs have written instructions (a "letter of instruction")?
items.detail: A document that says what exists, where things are, and what to do – without containing any seed words itself.
items.action: Write a letter of instruction: inventory, locations, contacts – never seed phrases. Store it with your will or attorney.

items.question: Are your keys geographically separated?
items.detail: Never all backups in one home. Fire, theft or flood should never be able to destroy access.
items.action: Move one key/backup to a second location: bank vault, trusted family, or a professional key agent.

items.question: Does at least one heir know your bitcoin exists and where to start?
items.detail: Bitcoin discovered years late, or never, is the most common inheritance failure.
items.action: Tell one trusted person the outline exists and who to contact. Full details only in the letter of instruction.

items.question: Do you use multisig (2-of-3) instead of a single seed phrase?
items.detail: A single seed is a single point of failure – for you and for your heirs.
items.action: Upgrade to 2-of-3 multisig: you hold two keys, a partner (e.g. Unchained-style vault) or attorney holds one.

items.question: Have you tested recovery with a small amount?
items.detail: An untested inheritance procedure is a hypothesis, not a plan.
items.action: Do a full recovery drill on a small UTXO, with your heir watching, once a year.

items.question: Are exchange accounts, loans and automated plans documented?
items.detail: Custodial balances, bitcoin-backed loans and DCA bots die with forgotten logins.
items.action: Maintain an inventory of platforms, account IDs and how balances should be claimed – inside your letter of instruction.
